O formato nativo do MuJoCo. O scene.xml: MuJoCo's native format. Menagerie's scene.xml includes g1.xml (bodies, joints, meshes, actuators, sensors, and the "stand" pose) and adds floor, sky, and light. URDF, the ROS format, also opens in MuJoCo, but it doesn't describe actuators or sensors the way MJCF does.
mujoco.MjModel.from_xml_path lê o XML, c: mujoco.MjModel.from_xml_path reads the XML, loads the meshes from the assets folder, and computes masses, inertias, and addresses. Path or attribute errors show up here, before any step.
MjModel é o corpo e não muda durante a s: MjModel is the body and doesn't change during the simulation. MjData is the state: positions (qpos), velocities (qvel), commands (ctrl), sensor readings. Every script in the course reads one and writes to the other.
Cada mj_step avança 2 ms no G1 do Menage: Each mj_step advances 2 ms on the Menagerie G1 (implicitfast integrator). One second of simulation is 500 steps; on CPU, the G1 standing still runs much faster than real time.
Ficha do fabricante e arquivo podem dive: The maker's spec sheet and the file can differ: lesson 8 teaches you to note the difference.
Os três números que você vai ler em todo: The three numbers you'll read on every humanoid
A base do humanoide não está presa ao ch: The humanoid's base is not fixed to the ground: it is a free joint with 7 numbers (x, y, z and a 4-number quaternion for orientation).
Adding the 29 articulated joints gives 36. That is the size of qpos.
A base livre tem 6 velocidades (3 linear: The free base has 6 velocities (3 linear and 3 angular), one fewer than the 7 positions, because the quaternion has 4 numbers for 3 rotations.
6 + 29 = 35. É o tamanho de qvel e de qa: 6 + 29 = 35. That is the size of qvel and qacc.
Um atuador por junta articulada. A base: One actuator per articulated joint. The base has no motor: the robot only moves by pushing against the ground with its feet.
Na versão com mãos (scene_with_hands.xml: In the version with hands (scene_with_hands.xml) the number goes up to 43. The G1 on sale has between 23 and 43 degrees of freedom depending on the version; the Menagerie ships the 29 one.
Humanoide com base livre: nq = nu + 7 e: Humanoid with a free base: nq = nu + 7 and nv = nu + 6, when each joint has one motor.

A média das posições de todos os corpos,: The average of all body positions, weighted by mass. MuJoCo computes it in d.subtree_com; the pelvis one is the whole robot's. At rest, the G1's sits 0.69 m above the floor (lesson 8).
O menor polígono convexo que contém todo: The smallest convex polygon that contains every point of the feet touching the ground with force. With both feet on the ground, it is the area between them; with one foot on its toes, it shrinks to a line.

O centro de pressão é o ponto médio dos: The center of pressure is the midpoint of the contacts, weighted by the normal force. On flat ground, it coincides with the ZMP of classical controllers. It never leaves the polygon: when it touches the edge, the foot starts to rotate.
CoM fora do apoio por um instante não de: CoM outside the support for a moment does not knock it over: the robot rotates over the edge of the foot and can come back. What knocks it over is rotating too fast to come back. The script calls it a fall when the pelvis is below 0.5 m at t = 3 s.
Parado, basta o CoM dentro do apoio. Em: Standing still, it is enough for the CoM to be inside the support. In motion, the CoP and the speed are what matter.

O CoM nunca sai do polígono: a margem nã: The CoM never leaves the polygon: the margin never goes negative at any moment.
É o que qualquer pose rígida aguenta: o: That is what any rigid pose can handle: the impulse is small (3 N·s).
O robô sobe na ponta dos pés, o polígono: The robot rises onto its toes, the polygon becomes a line, and the CoM is outside it for a moment. Even so, it comes back and ends up standing.
Sair do apoio não é cair: é começar a gi: Leaving the support is not falling: it is starting to rotate.
Com 40 N o CoM sai em t = 0,73 s; o robô: At 40 N the CoM leaves at t = 0.73 s; the robot sways forward, comes back, overshoots, and falls backward, without moving a foot.
